_comment: CURATED SPECIMEN (BL-123, decision D-10 option A). Copied from the producer's own example translations with ONE field changed: `decisions`. Everything else is the producer's, so the section stays consistent with the store it was rendered from. THE CURATION RULE, applied identically to every section: a board ask stays only where a DATE or a BREACHED THRESHOLD forces it this quarter. Everything else the CISO speaks to. Asks were DROPPED, never re-pitched from board to management to get under the number — assemble_pack.py:485 names that failure and it would be the dishonest way to hit five. ——— THIS SECTION: R-007 kept: a Critical residual OVER APPETITE is a breached threshold. R-006 dropped: it is currently WITHIN appetite on a patch alone, so it is next quarter's argument, not this sitting's decision.
executiveSummary: Two of our eleven tracked risks sit above the appetite the board set, down from three at the Q3 review — the direction is right, but the composition changed. Ransomware exposure through the internet-facing VPN appliance came down after an emergency patch and is now within appetite. Payment fraud moved the other way: two further supplier-invoice fraud attempts landed this quarter and email authentication is still not enforcing, so that risk rose from High to Critical and now sits alongside the third-party CRM exposure. Two accepted risks passed their re-validation date and need the board to either renew or withdraw the acceptance, and two risks are past their scheduled review. We are asking for two decisions today: fund DMARC enforcement to close the payment-fraud path, and renew or withdraw the two lapsed acceptances.

risks.R-003: A breach at the CRM vendor would expose customer records we do not directly control. The insurance rider moves the financial loss but not the regulatory notification duty or the customer-facing consequence, so this stays above appetite regardless of the transfer.
risks.R-007: An attacker impersonating a supplier can redirect a live payment before anyone notices. Two attempts landed this quarter; callback verification caught both, but that control is a person on a phone, not a system. Until email authentication enforces, the next attempt only has to beat one person having a bad day.
risks.R-006: An unpatched internet-facing appliance is the most direct route to enterprise-wide ransomware. The emergency patch closed the immediate path and brought this within appetite; the network segmentation that would keep it there is still unfunded.
risks.R-008: Regulated customer data can leave through unmanaged endpoints with no detective control in the path, and the risk has no named owner — which means nobody is accountable for closing it.
risks.R-001: Stolen administrator credentials are the difference between an incident and an outage. Privileged access management has already cut the blast radius; this is now a managed risk rather than an open one.

themes.identity: Identity is where our exposure grew this quarter — payment fraud outweighed the gains from privileged access management.
themes.third-party: Vendor exposure is unchanged and remains our single largest residual risk.

decisions.text: Fund DMARC enforcement and supplier bank-detail verification to bring payment fraud (R-007) back within appetite, or record the board's acceptance of a Critical residual.
